comment: Roadmap item 74. One entry per required test case. `runner` must exist in the repo; `check_test_matrix.py` enforces that, and enforces that `status` is one of the honest values below. Never mark a case `running` unless the named runner actually executes it today.

status_values.running: executes today, either as a host test or against a real browser binary in this repo
status_values.needs-build: the harness exists but needs a Chromium/Bedrock build to produce a verdict
status_values.needs-network: requires a live external service (only the Tor network), never run in CI by default

cases.note: binary starts and reports a version
local page loads, scripting runs, URL matches
two command-line URLs become two live page targets; tab model logic is covered by ui/tab_model_test.cc
page-initiated download lands in the configured directory; naming/collision logic in downloads/download_manager_test.cc
state persists in one profile and is absent in a fresh one
measurable today against stock Chromium (baseline recorded); the pass criterion is a Bedrock build
filter engine + heuristic through the full pipeline
policy side is host-tested in privacy/fingerprinting/fingerprint_policy_test.cc
the header the third party receives is recorded by the local server
key derivation is host-tested in privacy/storage/storage_isolation_test.cc
policy host test: privacy/network/webrtc_policy_test.cc
no query is ever sent to Google in tests
malformed provider strings are also fuzzed: fuzz/search_fuzzer.cc
permission parsing is fuzzed: fuzz/extension_permission_fuzzer.cc
loading a real unpacked extension requires a Chromium build; procedure documented in MATRIX.md until then
per-extension host access rules
requires a running tor daemon; no daemon is bundled yet (open decision in .ai/memory/STATE.md)
what a New Identity clears, without the network
asserts DNS is not resolved locally when a SOCKS proxy is in use
contrast ratios and focus order; screen-reader verification stays manual
every command has a reachable shortcut and focus order is complete
